files.purpose: Introduces Hafþi OS, its current limitations, and how to download, build and test it.
files.when: Read before trying the prototype or making your first build.
details: The image is an x86_64 live USB with an offline whole-disk installer. Installation erases exactly the disk reviewed and confirmed by the user.
Documents account setup, BIOS/UEFI boot, settings persistence, lack of Secure Boot/custom partitions/dual boot, and the graphical password login.
Downloads contain an ISO, checksum, measured size, file register and VM diagnostics.

files.purpose: Keeps generated build output, VM screenshots and Python bytecode out of version control.
files.when: Git uses it when deciding which untracked files to offer for staging.
details: out/ contains ISO builds and test output. preview/ contains downloaded VM diagnostics.
__pycache__/ and *.pyc are generated by Python.
Ignoring a path does not delete it and does not remove a file that was already committed.

files.purpose: Runs the automated checks, builds the ISO, boots a disposable VM and uploads download artifacts.
files.when: GitHub Actions runs it for pushes to main or a manual workflow dispatch.
details: The runner is Ubuntu; the image is built inside a privileged Arch Linux container because Archiso needs mount operations.
The container installs Archiso, GRUB and Python, then builds from the official baseline profile.
The output is handed back to the runner for the VM test. The VM uses a temporary virtual disk, not a host disk.
hafthiOS-prototype contains the ISO; hafthiOS-preview contains the screenshot, serial log and size report. Artifacts currently expire after 14 days.
A successful build and BIOS VM test do not establish compatibility with every graphics card, wireless device, UEFI firmware or Secure Boot setup.

Test-script-only corrections can retest an unchanged ISO from the same repository using iso_run_id or [retest-iso:RUN_ID]. The artifact records the original build run in iso-source.txt; embedded source snapshots remain those of the original ISO.

A reused-ISO retest may use KVM for disk installation and BIOS/UEFI boot, falling back to TCG. Ship animation and Esc toggling are checked by the full TCG build. Failed VM screens are captured and OCR text is written to diagnostics.
The packages job must pass actual git/base-devel installation in an extracted OS root before the iso job can run. It exports hafthiOS-pacman-test logs.

files.purpose: Builds the bootable live ISO and embeds the offline file guide and source snapshots.
files.when: Run as root on an Arch build host; CI runs it inside its build container.
details: Copies /usr/share/archiso/configs/baseline into a temporary build workspace. It does not edit the system-wide baseline.
Copies live/ into the image root and installs the guide under /usr/share/doc/hafthios/.
Packages include Niri, Cage, GTK, Fish, Mesa and Vulkan drivers, network tools, browser runtime dependencies and fonts. The pinned Hafþi binary is compiled before packaging.
Sets Hafþi OS branding and uses SquashFS with xz compression. Adds executable permissions for the two session programs.
Enables NetworkManager in the live image, then invokes mkarchiso to produce out/*.iso.
Writes a SHA256 checksum and size.txt. A marketed 1 GB USB target means less than 1,000,000,000 bytes.
The temporary build workspace is removed on exit. No selected installation disk is partitioned, formatted or mounted.

Installs Plymouth, applies the quiet boot configuration, and masks the default early quit/wait services. The tty1 getty releases Plymouth with retain-splash just before starting the graphical session.
Packages and validates the full ISO file register with package-inventory.py before calculating the final ISO checksum.
Includes common Intel, AMD, Atheros, Realtek and Broadcom firmware, Wi-Fi authentication and PipeWire audio. Hardware support still requires real-device testing.
Includes rsync, arch-install-scripts, GRUB and filesystem tools for an offline installed-system copy.
Enables hafthios-package-keys.service to initialize package signing trust before the first desktop login.

files.purpose: Checks that every project file has a guide entry, then bundles the guide and an exact copy of each documented source file.
files.when: During ISO creation; it can also be run directly for a local documentation check.
details: The repository file inventory excludes Git internals, generated output, downloaded previews and Python bytecode.
Missing explanations stop the bundle build, so a new project file cannot silently disappear from the guide.
Copies documented source files into sources/ while preserving their relative paths. The reader never executes these snapshots.
Rejects absolute paths and parent-directory traversal in the catalog.
The disk installer copies the same documentation directory into the installed system.

files.purpose: Boots the ISO, validates the welcome and complete guide, then opens Niri, Hafþi and Google Chrome in a disposable VM.
files.when: After a successful image build in GitHub Actions.
details: Uses CPU emulation, 4 GB RAM, accelerated VirtIO graphics backed by host Mesa, and a disposable 16 GiB sparse disk.
Waits for HAFTHIOS_GUI_READY in the serial log, then saves the welcome screenshot.
Sends F1 through QEMU to open the offline guide and waits for HAFTHIOS_GUIDE_READY.
Captures diagnostics on failure and terminates the VM when the test ends.
This is a BIOS VM smoke test. It is not a destructive installation test or a real-hardware certification.

Detects the ship splash in screenshots before GTK starts, checks that frames change, presses Esc and verifies the ship artwork disappears for details, then verifies the second Esc restores the ship. Also checks the welcome screen and F1 guide as before.
Requires the complete register ready marker and more than 1,000 filesystem entries when the guide opens.
Presses F2 to enter Niri, requires the exact Hafþi application ID in the compositor window list, opens Chrome setup through Super+B, and waits for the browser window after an actual download.
Captures the actual SDL window inside Xvfb, because OpenGL scanouts may have no CPU image for QMP screendump. QMP remains responsible for keyboard input.
Also opens the language and keyboard page using F3 and saves settings-screen.ppm before returning to the guide and desktop.
After testing the live desktop, drives the VM console to install onto its newly created disposable 16 GiB disk. The ISO contains no automatic installer test service.
Detaches the ISO, boots the disk under BIOS and OVMF UEFI, logs in with a throwaway test password and verifies persisted Swedish settings, ext4 root and removal of live privileges.
Installs git and base-devel with pacman -Syu in the live VM, validates their executables, and then copies that system to disk.
Waits for a newly created focused Hafthi window rather than accepting a stale focus report before typing the package/installation test script.
Waits for the live text login prompt and verifies the complete username before submitting it, so a console startup race cannot silently drop its first character.
Sends complete QMP key chords with non-overlapping release timers and uses a virtio network adapter in the disposable VMs. Kernel messages may wrap the echoed login username onto a new line.
Boots the ISO written to a writable 32 GiB virtual USB. This reproduces physical USB copy-to-RAM boot while keeping a separate empty 16 GiB installation disk and read-only test CD.

files.purpose: Makes the live image log in automatically on its first virtual console.
files.when: systemd starts getty@tty1 while the live ISO boots.
details: The empty ExecStart= clears the original getty command. The next ExecStart= launches agetty with --autologin hafthi.
%I expands to the instance name, tty1. --noclear keeps the existing console contents.
This setting is for the disposable live image. It must not be copied unchanged into an installed desktop.
ExecStartPre asks Plymouth to quit while retaining its last frame, releasing graphics before Cage starts. A missing or unavailable Plymouth is nonfatal.

files.purpose: Documents that root does not start the graphical live session.
files.when: Read when inspecting login profiles.
details: The graphical tty1 session now autologins as hafthi rather than root.

files.purpose: Sets up the live graphical environment and launches the welcome application inside Cage.
files.when: Called by the live login profile on tty1.
details: Starts Cage for the welcome screen as the ordinary live user.
Try the desktop sets a runtime marker; after Cage exits, this script starts niri-session.
Only Cage receives WLR_RENDERER=pixman. Niri uses accelerated graphics; failures print its user journal for diagnosis.
Keeps local session logs and restores the welcome screen after the desktop exits.
On process or systemd service failure, captures Niri diagnostics and opens the graphics error page. It loads live language/layout settings on each transition.

files.purpose: Implements the live welcome screen, reviewed whole-disk installation, desktop controls and offline guide reader.
files.when: Cage launches it on live boot. Run hafthios-welcome --guide to open the guide directly.
details: read_disks uses the read-only lsblk JSON query. It lists writable whole disks and excludes partitions, loop devices and read-only devices.
Network settings launches nmtui in Foot for the live session. Restart calls systemctl reboot.
The guide is read from /usr/share/doc/hafthios/. A search field filters file names and explanations; each article can show its bundled source snapshot.
F1 opens the guide. Serial markers are used by the VM test to verify that the UI and guide loaded.
The guide source viewer recognises binary assets and displays an explanation instead of attempting to show image bytes as UTF-8 text.

The guide defaults to the complete ISO file register. Queries the read-only SQLite database by path, package or image layer, renders 100 rows per page and provides Previous/Next controls. The source guide remains a separate view.
Adds independent English/Swedish interface language and US/Swedish keyboard choices, plus asynchronous network status and configuration.
A scrollable content area keeps controls reachable in small VM windows. A failed desktop shows actual local diagnostics.
Install Hafthi OS lists eligible unmounted disks, requests a root-owned plan, reviews full-disk erasure and requires matching passwords and the exact erase phrase.
Installation runs in a worker with JSON progress. Passwords are passed through stdin, not command arguments or log messages. Close and navigation are blocked while writing.
The installed desktop omits the installer button; its ready marker reports root filesystem and persistent settings for the VM test.

The desktop uses GTK4 Layer Shell to anchor a single panel to the right edge. Hide panel leaves a small clickable edge tab; Super+Shift+Space toggles the same instance; Super+Space opens the program launcher. The user's hidden state is saved separately.
Display settings lists Niri's advertised modes and scaling. A trial has a 15-second confirmation countdown plus an independent restore process if the GUI crashes. Only confirmed settings are written.
Displays the installer backend JSON error when preparing installation fails, rather than hiding the cause behind a subprocess exit status.

Disk listing and installation planning both run through the privileged installer helper; probing the original USB after RAM boot requires block-device access. Backend errors and sudo failures are shown to the user.

files.purpose: Tests the read-only disk discovery helpers without needing a GTK display.
files.when: Run with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v.
details: Checks exclusion of partitions, loop devices, optical media and read-only disks.
Mocks lsblk to check disk size formatting and that only the intended read-only query is executed.
Checks the empty-disk case. These tests do not validate physical hardware or perform installation.
Verifies the real installation UI lists disks through sudo and the read-only installer action, preserving JSON backend failures and sudo errors.

files.purpose: Tests catalog coverage, source snapshot packaging and rejection of unsafe catalog paths.
files.when: As part of the normal Python tests before ISO creation.
details: Checks that every project file is documented and each connection points to a known file.
Builds a temporary guide bundle and compares its source snapshots to the repository files.
Tests that a catalog path cannot escape the bundle directory.

files.purpose: Explains how to use the file guide and the scope of the local documentation.
files.when: Read on GitHub or through the bundled source viewer.
details: The guide documents the project-owned files, not every file provided by Arch packages.
The local bundle includes the guide and source snapshots matching that ISO build.
The live session is ephemeral. The disk installer copies this documentation bundle to the target system.

files.purpose: Stores one English article for every project-owned file, including this catalog itself.
files.when: The bundler validates it; the GTK guide reader displays it locally.
details: Each article records path, purpose, when it runs, connected files and detailed behavior.
Keep entries consistent with the implementation when changing code. Catalog coverage checks cannot verify the truth of prose automatically.
The catalog is data only. The reader displays its text and does not execute commands from articles.

files.purpose: Brands and quiets the BIOS, UEFI and loopback boot entries.
files.when: While assembling the Archiso profile before mkarchiso runs.
details: Adds quiet splash parameters, enables status collection behind the splash, and prevents deferred framebuffer-console takeover from leaving a stale ship frame in the details view. Retains the official live-medium discovery and loopback arguments. Hides the short UEFI menu, shortens the BIOS menu, and brands entries as Hafthi OS.
Fails if the expected boot entries are absent rather than silently producing an image without the splash. Running it twice does not duplicate parameters.
Allocates up to half the RAM to the disposable copy-on-write layer so the first-use Chrome download and extraction fit. Space is consumed as needed, not preallocated.

files.purpose: Checks that quiet boot preserves the arguments needed to find the live ISO.
files.when: During local validation and the CI check step.
details: Uses representative BIOS, UEFI and loopback entries. Verifies discovery arguments survive, quiet parameters appear once, and missing baseline entries fail clearly.

files.purpose: Starts graphics and Plymouth in the live image initramfs.
files.when: Before the main live filesystem is mounted.
details: Keeps the official Archiso discovery hooks and adds kms, keyboard and plymouth after udev. Explicitly loads the PS/2 and USB keyboard drivers before starting Plymouth. The kms hook includes graphics drivers and the keyboard hook makes Esc available before the live filesystem is mounted; Plymouth draws the ship while the live system starts.

files.purpose: Selects the Hafþi OS splash without a display delay.
files.when: When Plymouth starts in the initramfs and during live boot.
details: Theme=hafthios selects the project theme. ShowDelay=0 shows it as soon as the graphics device becomes available.

files.purpose: Registers the ship splash with the Plymouth script renderer.
files.when: When Plymouth loads the selected theme.
details: Points to the script and its artwork directory using paths available in the live image and initramfs.

files.purpose: Animates the supplied ship artwork on a dark boot screen.
files.when: From early live boot until the graphical session takes over.
details: Scales the image proportionally to fit the screen. A refresh callback moves it gently sideways and vertically, suggesting a quiet voyage. The original artwork stays intact.
Shows an Esc hint. Plymouth itself handles Esc to switch between the graphical theme and boot details; this script does not intercept or discard logs.

files.purpose: Contains the user-supplied white Viking ship artwork on a dark background.
files.when: Loaded by the Plymouth theme during startup.
details: A PNG format conversion of the supplied JPEG, preserving its decoded pixels and proportions. This is a binary image, not a text source file.

files.purpose: Indexes every entry in the live root, ISO filesystem, early/main initramfs and EFI FAT image.
files.when: During ISO construction and final verification.
details: Walks all entries without following symbolic links, including dotfiles, broken links, directories and special nodes. Reads exact live-system package owner/version/description from pacman manifests. Records type, size, mode, UID/GID and link target. Unix permissions and ownership are left unassigned for the EFI FAT layer because FAT does not store them.
Labels project explanations, package metadata, location-based inference and unverified roles distinctly. Other image layers do not claim live-system package ownership merely because paths match.

Creates a paginated SQLite register, including the register itself, and exports the final records as CSV. Embedded compressed-container size is intentionally unknown until packaging; the exported final register records the actual size. Coverage verification compares every layer/path/type with the final ISO.

files.purpose: Embeds and verifies the complete ISO file register.
files.when: After Archiso creates the first ISO.
details: Extracts the ISO with xorriso, early/main initramfs with lsinitcpio, and the EFI FAT image with mtools. Generates the embedded database in the actual prepared root filesystem.

Invalidates only the SquashFS and ISO build checkpoints and repacks, reusing package installation and boot images. Extracts the finished ISO and SquashFS to independently verify full path/type coverage against the embedded register. Exports SQLite, CSV and layer counts beside the ISO.

files.purpose: Verifies inventory coverage, package ownership and self-indexing.
files.when: During local validation and GitHub Actions.
details: Checks dotfiles, dangling symlinks, directory symlinks without traversal, exact metadata ownership, stable register self-size and absence of transient SQLite journal entries. Verifies missing entries are rejected by the final coverage checker.

files.purpose: Builds the Hafþi terminal from a pinned upstream source revision.
files.when: During the Arch ISO build.
details: Compiles the MIT-licensed terminal with Rust and places the executable, command helper, license and source revision in the image.
Build dependencies live in the isolated build container. Cargo dependency resolution follows the upstream manifest, which currently has no committed lockfile.
Applies the reviewed OS horizontal edge-resize patch to the pinned revision before compilation; git apply failures stop the build.

files.purpose: Creates the ordinary live-session user and validates the Niri configuration.
files.when: Archiso runs this customization hook after package installation.
details: The hafthi account is UID 1000 and owns its disposable home. Autologin is limited to tty1.
The live user can administer the live session through sudo; this policy must not be copied to an installed system.
Generates en_US.UTF-8 and sv_SE.UTF-8 locales in the image.
Validates real Niri configurations for English/US, Swedish/Swedish and English/Swedish without changing the live user defaults.
Fails the build if core or extra has no active HTTPS package server.

files.purpose: Starts the graphical welcome from the live user’s tty1 login.
files.when: When the autologin shell starts.
details: The guard prevents graphical startup inside Hafþi or another terminal.
A session environment marker prevents recursion when niri-session starts a login shell.
Loads the live locale environment for new Bash login shells before checking the welcome TTY.

files.purpose: Grants administrative commands in the disposable live session.
files.when: When the live wheel user invokes sudo.
details: No password is required in the live session.
Do not reuse this live-only policy on a disk installation.

files.purpose: Defines the minimal Niri desktop and keyboard shortcuts.
files.when: When Try the desktop starts Niri.
details: Starts Hafþi and the desktop controls. Defines focus, window management, browser and guide shortcuts.
Uses the system’s accelerated graphics driver, not the welcome compositor’s software renderer.
Terminal actions use the locale-aware wrapper. Super + comma opens language and keyboard settings.
Super+Space opens the native launcher; Super+Shift+Space toggles the right panel. Super+right-button dragging remains available for compositor window resizing.

files.purpose: Downloads and opens official Google Chrome without bundling its executable in the ISO.
files.when: When Open Google Chrome is selected for the first time.
details: Downloads over HTTPS directly from Google and extracts the official Debian package into the live user home.
Shows Google’s terms and an explicit download button. Download work runs in a background thread; failures allow retry.
Runs as a normal user with the namespace sandbox enabled. Does not use --no-sandbox or write to a target disk.

files.purpose: Checks Chrome sandbox policy and failed-download recovery.
files.when: Local and CI checks before an ISO build.
details: Rejects launching Chrome as root; verifies ordinary-user launches retain sandbox protections.
Simulates an offline download and verifies existing browser files are preserved and temporary files cleaned.

files.purpose: Validates and applies the ordinary live user's language and keyboard choices.
files.when: When Apply is clicked in Language and keyboard, or when its CLI is used.
details: Display modes are obtained from niri msg --json outputs. Trials reject modes not advertised by the selected connected output, start an independent restore watchdog, then apply mode and scale through Niri IPC.
Confirmed modes and scales are stored in displays.json and appended to the validated user Niri configuration. Language changes preserve these display settings.
Only English/Swedish locales and US/Swedish keyboard layouts are accepted. Language and layout are independent.
Niri validates a temporary configuration before the current user configuration is atomically replaced. Niri watches that file to reload the keyboard.
The helper writes settings.json and a shell environment file in the user home. It does not mount or modify a target disk.

files.purpose: Starts Hafthi with the currently selected live-session locale.
files.when: Niri autostart and terminal shortcuts launch this wrapper.
details: Loads the generated language and keyboard environment from the live home, then replaces itself with Hafthi.
Changing language affects newly launched terminals, rather than changing the environment of existing processes.

files.purpose: Checks live settings validation and recovery after a failed desktop launch.
files.when: The test suite runs locally and in the ISO build workflow.
details: Uses temporary homes to verify independent language/layout choices, actual shell environment loading, and preservation of previous files after validation fails.
Malformed settings and unsupported values are rejected or replaced with documented defaults.
Mocks compositor and systemd commands to verify that both process failures and failed service results reopen the welcome screen with diagnostics.

files.purpose: Plans and performs an explicitly confirmed offline installation to one entire disk.
files.when: The welcome UI calls list/plan; a confirmed install invokes it through sudo.
details: Eligible targets are canonical, unmounted, writable whole disks of at least 12 GiB without mounted/stacked descendants. The live medium is mounted and excluded.
Root-only plans expire after 30 minutes and bind disk path, size, model, serial, WWN and device number. Exact typed confirmation and a valid password are checked again before writes.
Creates BIOS boot, EFI and ext4 partitions, copies the live root and home, installs normal kernel/initramfs/GRUB and retains the offline ISO guide.
Removes live autologin and passwordless sudo, locks root, sets the hafthi password through stdin, and applies the saved language/layout to the installed home.
A single-instance lock and consumed plans prevent concurrent/repeated execution. Errors stop installation and may leave the confirmed disk partially written.

Recognizes the actual Archiso overlay and read-only squashfs root with or without mounted boot media. Resolves original USB identity from Archiso UUID/label/device arguments and excludes it after copy-to-RAM; refuses disk selection if live media cannot be identified. Requests an explicit lsblk tree so partition UUIDs exclude the whole USB parent even without a NAME column.

files.purpose: Exercises installer disk-selection and confirmation boundaries without writing real disks.
files.when: Runs locally and in the ISO workflow.
details: Tests exclusion of live media, mounted roots, swap, readonly/small disks and stacked devices.
Checks exact confirmation, password constraints, expiry and changed disk identity. Invalid confirmation cannot reach a disk-writing command.

Uses a temporary target tree to verify removal of live autologin/NOPASSWD and replacement with normal installed kernel and locale settings. The actual install/boot path is exercised in a disposable VM.

Checks RAM and USB live-root recognition, rejects installed or unrelated roots, excludes an unmounted USB by boot UUID, and fails closed when live media identity or the verified live root is missing. Reproduces flat lsblk JSON without NAME and verifies explicit tree output excludes the USB parent.

files.purpose: Provides an active HTTPS Arch package mirror for core and extra.
files.when: Used by pacman and Yay in the live session and after disk installation.
details: Uses the geographically routed geo.mirror.pkgbuild.com server with literal $repo and $arch placeholders.
The live filesystem copy preserves this configuration on disk. Package signature checking is unchanged.

files.purpose: Initializes the local trusted Arch package keyring before the desktop is available.
files.when: First boot of a live or installed system without its successful keyring marker.
details: Runs pacman-key --init and --populate archlinux as root, using the bundled Arch trust data.
Creates a completion marker only after both commands succeed; failed initialization can retry at the next boot.
Retained on disk installation. Package signature checks remain required.

files.purpose: Performs real signed package installations before permitting a new ISO build.
files.when: The packages CI job, in an isolated privileged Arch container.
details: Extracts the existing Hafthi OS SquashFS into a temporary filesystem; host disks are not selected or formatted.
Applies the pending mirror configuration, discards only the disposable root keyring, then runs the exact key initialization commands from the shipped service.
Requires trusted package signatures, runs a full pacman upgrade with git and base-devel, executes git and make, then verifies a second signed git installation.
The ISO job depends on this successful test. Extracted test files are removed on exit.

files.purpose: Styles the native coastal greeter with quiet typography and restrained input controls.
files.when: Used during installed password login.
details: No session chooser, visible command paths, image rectangle or large bordered panel.
Uses muted sage controls and readable field focus, error messages and animation-pause control.

files.purpose: Hands Plymouth over to greetd on installed systems and prevents tty1 conflicts.
files.when: Used during installed password login.
details: The live trial session keeps its existing welcome screen.
Password authentication is performed by greetd and the system PAM configuration.

files.purpose: Starts the authenticated Niri session with saved language and keyboard settings.
files.when: Used during installed password login.
details: The live trial session keeps its existing welcome screen.
Password authentication is performed by greetd and the system PAM configuration.

files.purpose: Installs and validates Hafthi OS on the CI-created disposable VM disk.
files.when: Run as root only from the separate temporary read-only test CD.
details: Requires the explicit --disposable-vm argument and uses the normal live installer with its disk confirmation checks.
Tests signed package transactions, installs to /dev/vda and reports progress over the VM serial console.
It is never embedded in the distributable ISO or attached to installed BIOS/UEFI boot tests.

Requires a RAM-backed live root with bootmnt unmounted and only the disposable disk eligible before installation. Emits HAFTHIOS_RAM_USB_INSTALL_TEST_OK alongside full installation and desktop checks.

files.purpose: Draws a quiet animated coast and authenticates the installed user through greetd and PAM.
files.when: Cage launches it at installed boot and after logout.
details: Native GTK fields support password masking and repeated PAM prompts. Socket exchanges run off the drawing thread; no credentials are logged or persisted.
Only a successful greetd authentication can launch the fixed installed session command. Preview mode never authenticates or launches a session.
Cairo draws slow wave fronts, shore, two gulls and the original Plymouth ship. Pause waves or F10 stops motion.

files.purpose: Checks greetd framing and the authentication state machine without GTK or a real account.
files.when: The unit suite runs before each ISO build.
details: Exercises fragmented Unicode replies, closed sockets, masked secret prompts, failed authentication, repeated PAM messages and the fixed session command.
A start-session acknowledgement is required before the greeter exits.

files.purpose: Renders the native coastal greeter under Xvfb before ISO construction.
files.when: GitHub Actions runs this after unit checks.
details: Captures a real GTK screenshot and fails on GTK diagnostics or an early exit.
Checks that waves change between frames and freeze after F10. Preview cannot authenticate or launch a desktop.

files.purpose: Draws a quiet living Viking village behind the Niri desktop.
files.when: Starts with each live or installed desktop session.
details: Native GTK4 background-layer surfaces on each monitor receive no keyboard or pointer input. Cairo reuses the original ship and draws waves, construction, workers, fishing, hunting and trade routes.

Smoothed aggregate CPU load and received network bytes influence village activity. Recognized CPU temperature sensors influence lighting; unavailable VM sensors remain unknown. No network requests or per-application data are collected.
The panel stores enable, pause, economy and responsiveness preferences in ~/.config/hafthios/world.json. Village age is saved every 30 seconds in ~/.local/state/hafthios/world.json.

Animation uses at most 12 frames per second, 8 under high load and 5 in economy mode or on low battery. Pause freezes village age and telemetry appearance; settings continue to be polled. Runtime status supports actual VM verification.

The 2160×1350 scene uses uniform fitting on every display. Adults, doorways, longhouses and ships share scene units; ship scale excludes the original PNG margins and its hull is anchored at the waterline.

Continuous occupation routes lead from a house doorway to woodcutting, hunting, animal feeding, construction, shipbuilding, cargo work and smithing, then back indoors. Docked voyage intervals allow animated loading; the boatyard grows a hull and launches a new ship. A forge includes hearth glow, bellows and anvil work.

Shared schedules connect a timber delivery to smithing, tool delivery and shipwright work. The hull gains planks after tools arrive and launches after the builders finish. A separate arrival clock brings two crew members over the gangplank, unloads cargo by cart at the market and boards them before departure. Helper counts still respond to CPU activity.

The slightly wider view includes fields, grain storage, fish delivery, cooking, bread, net repair, sail weaving, roof repair, herded goats, chickens, conversation, benches and shared supper. A continuous saved 30-minute day brings villagers home, dims the sky and reveals sparse stars; clouds move slowly.

files.purpose: Renders and checks the real village drawing before the ISO build.
files.when: Runs in the greeter CI job or locally with Cairo and Pillow.
details: Creates start, moving, paused and busy village PNGs using the same Cairo drawing function used on the desktop.
Checks that animation and telemetry change pixels, identical paused timestamps render identically and the sky stays dark. Reports the measured render time without assuming GPU acceleration.

files.purpose: Tests village telemetry, preferences and power-saving decisions.
files.when: Runs with the project unittest suite before the ISO build.
details: Synthetic proc/sys files verify smoothed CPU/network counters, loopback exclusion, CPU-only temperature readings, missing sensors and low battery.
Checks preference validation and reduced frame cadence; the separate VM test exercises the actual GTK background and pause/resume behavior.
Checks continuous worker journeys into and out of homes and voyage continuity with real docking intervals for cargo work.
Verifies handoff order, crew boarding before departure and position continuity across two full connected-work cycles.

files.purpose: Native GTK program search overlay launched on demand.
files.when: During desktop use or build verification.
details: Discovers visible desktop entries with Gio, ranks up to five results and launches through AppInfo without shell parsing.
Saves only recent desktop-entry IDs; supports keyboard arrows, Enter, Escape and outside click. The layer-shell overlay dims the village and releases keyboard focus on exit.

files.purpose: Registers Hafthi in program launchers.
files.when: During desktop use or build verification.
details: Uses the existing terminal wrapper and a standard terminal icon.

files.purpose: Registers Chrome and its first-use download wrapper.
files.when: During desktop use or build verification.
details: Launching this entry opens Chrome or the existing download dialog.

files.purpose: Adds horizontal edge dragging to the pinned Hafthi terminal source.
files.when: During desktop use or build verification.
details: A six-logical-pixel left/right target uses winit Wayland drag_resize_window and a horizontal resize cursor.
Interior text selection remains unchanged; preferences and context menus do not trigger edge resizes.

files.purpose: Renders and tests the actual GTK launcher under Xvfb before an ISO build.
files.when: During desktop use or build verification.
details: Uses a temporary desktop entry to verify search, actual launch and Escape; saves a screenshot and diagnostics.

files.purpose: Checks launcher matching and bounded recent program history.
files.when: During desktop use or build verification.
details: Exercises accent folding, multiword search, name ranking, missing results, corrupt history and five-result limit.

files.purpose: Updates installed Hafthi-owned desktop files with backup and rollback.
files.when: During desktop update creation, installation or verification.
details: Requires a completed successful main-branch VM run for the published release.
Checks archive and per-file hashes; rejects unexpected paths and links.
Preserves user files, village age and settings; --rollback restores the previous desktop.
